cells.verb: holding steady under real weight, on your own supply
cells.place: in the open field before anything has been chosen
cells.ask: pick one hope and keep walking toward it past the point where it's comfortable — what comes back is a light that's yours because you grew it, not borrowed
cells.core:
You can carry weight before you know what it's for. Nothing's decided yet, there's no plan to lean on, and you're not collapsing into the first option just to have ground under you — you're standing in the open and holding, quietly, with what you've got. That's a rarer kind of strength than the kind that needs a reason.

It isn't finished, though. Strength that can hold anything is free to pick something. If you wanted, you could take one hope out of the pile and keep walking toward it after the easy part ends — and what would come back is a light you earned, not one you were handed.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold steady before you've chosen. That strength is free to pick a direction.

cells.tense: Future — bracing at a page that can't be written yet
cells.verb: clenching against hardship that hasn't arrived
cells.place: in a space where nothing has been decided
cells.ask: take one thing someone offers you without paying it back, or give one thing without keeping count — what comes back is holding that contains instead of crushes
cells.core:
You're gripping for a fight that hasn't come. Everything's still open — nothing's been chosen, nothing's gone wrong yet — and you've already set your jaw against it, treating a field of possibilities like a siege you'll have to survive alone. The bracing is real; the enemy isn't here.

The way out isn't to hold tighter. Let one exchange happen that you don't have to carry by yourself: take what someone hands you without squaring the debt, or hand something over without the ledger. The grip loosens, and what's left is a strength that can hold what comes without crushing what hasn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're braced for a hardship that hasn't shown up. The grip is costing you the open field.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you
cells.verb: setting the weight down and stepping back from the holding
cells.place: at the edge of a wide-open space you haven't walked into
cells.ask: let one person see what you carried and what it cost you — what comes back is a holding that contains without forcing
cells.core:
You've stopped trusting your own legs. Whatever you were carrying is behind you now, and you're still reading the result as the verdict on your strength. So the open space in front of you — nothing decided, everything possible — looks like more than you can bear, and you stay at the edge of it.

Trying to force the strength back on won't work; it's empty in there. What fills it is being seen. Let one person look at what you carried and what it took out of you, without asking them to fix it. Being witnessed lets the old weight finally set down as finished, and the holding comes back on its own — steady, without strain.
cells.sheetLine: You set the weight down and haven't picked up anything since.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing
cells.verb: already enduring the pressure, steadily, with your own resources
cells.place: in a wide-open space where you'd say nothing has started yet
cells.ask: name the one hope you've been quietly carrying this toward — what comes back is a holding you can feel the shape of, strong without clenching
cells.core:
You're already holding. There's real weight on you, nothing's settled, and you're standing under it steadily — but if someone asked, you'd say you're just waiting, just getting by, nothing's really happening yet. The strength is doing its job every day. The one person who won't credit it is you.

The simplest version of this is a hope, not a plan. Somewhere under the holding there's a direction you've been quietly carrying toward, and you haven't said so. Say what it is, once, plainly. Once you own what you're holding for, the holding becomes something you can feel — strong without having to clench.
cells.sheetLine: You're already holding steady. You just call it waiting.

flags.detail: "a while ago" — a cell knows no one's past
